newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Congress party takes back key dissidents.
newsitem.headline: India's Congress party takes back key dissidents.

text.p: India's Congress party revoked the expulsion of two key dissident leaders on Thursday after they resigned from Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's 13-member United Front alliance, a party spokesman said.
He said former ministers Arjun Singh and Narain Dutt Tiwari were taken back into the party more than a year after former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao ordered their explusion.
Tiwari, who became head of the breakaway All India Indira Congress (Tiwari) party, told a news conference last month that his group wanted to merge unconditionally with the parent body.
But the Congress response was delayed because of a leadership tussle within India's oldest political machine, involving its new president Sitaram Kesri.
Kesri became Congress president in September after Rao was forced to quit over a string of court cases against him.
The new leader was made the head of the Congress Parliamentary Party (CPP) earlier this month, after Rao was asked to resign from that post as well.

Kesri told the CPP meeting that elected him leader that Congress was not planning to withdraw its make-or-break support for Deve Gowda, despite frequent reports that Congress under his leadership was keen to topple the government.
Congress is sharply divided over the issue with some of its leaders suggesting it should join Deve Gowda's minority government rather than be a non-participant supporter.
Both Singh and Tiwari said last month that their resignation from the United Front did not mean they were opposed to the government.
"Our decision to integrate with the Congress is an earnest effort to make Congress a predominant force in the country," Singh said last month.
Kesri says he wants to welcome back all former Congressmen to the party as part of an effort to rejuvenate the group that suffered its worst ever election defeat in May last year.
